rows.description: A child chooses among handshake, high-five, hug or wave depending on comfort. A child has the right to decline a hug or kiss from anyone and can offer a wave or fist bump instead.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Welcoming a guest or new classmate [Expressing]
rows.description: A child says hello, offers a seat, shares a snack or shows the new student around. Warm welcoming teaches inclusion, and shy children can still welcome with a smile or wave.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child explains rules of a game or defines a word to show understanding. Clear explanation grows with practice, and asking why or how encourages depth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child learns to summarize a story in a few lines and clarify a muddled point. Adults model choosing key points and admitting when something was not clear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child asks did I do it right or repeats an instruction back to check. Adults treat it as effort to learn, not as lack of confidence, and answer with specifics.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child asks a friend are you okay when noticing sad or quiet behaviour. Kind inquiry shows care, and the friend may or may not want to answer yet.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child voices doubt, saying I think you are joking, or suspicion when a story does not add up. Suspicion is a cue to check facts, not a verdict about character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who says I get it or I am not sure learns to match confidence to knowledge. Admitting a gap and asking for help are strengths a supportive teacher rewards.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child may concede a point with okay, you are right or qualify with yes, but. Adults praise conceding gracefully and help the child not treat it as losing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child learns to say I see it differently instead of shouting or sulking. Modelling I disagree, and here is why shows disagreement is not rejection of the person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
